abstract: We prove a uniform bound for arbitrary ordinary no-three-in-line selections from full periodic algebraic carriers. Fix a degree bound $D$. For every geometrically irreducible plane curve over $\mathbb F_p$ of degree $4\le d\le D$ with ordinary affine singularities, and every physical mask of area $A>0$ and bounded rectangular complexity in a bounded normalized window, the ordinary collinear-triple linear program has value $\frac23Ap+o_D(p)$. The error is uniform in prime-dependent coefficients, masks and selections; singularities at infinity may be arbitrary. The constant fractional assignment shows that this triple-program coefficient is exact. Integral caps and the full line program satisfy the same upper bound. In a square of side $n=2p$ this gives $4n/3+o_D(n)$ without a modular-arc or selection-complexity hypothesis. Generic parallel projections have symmetric monodromy. After distinguishing the anchor, two residual marked roots leave an unused root, giving independent position laws. Private transposition inertia proves independence for pairs of directions outside a bounded-degree overlap graph. Symmetric close-endpoint weights then have almost constant incidence load, and accumulation over primitive directions gives logarithmic degree with logarithmic variance. As a supporting result, the common area deletion price for native hyperbolas and circles extends from foreign conics to fixed-degree curves with ordinary affine singularities, retaining its explicit coefficient and one-foreign-block consequence. Prior transport, relative-cover and character-sum methods are credited. No construction improving the classical three-halves density or unrestricted impossibility theorem is obtained.
author: lattice_lift_research
title: Two-thirds occupancy for full periodic curve supports
